en.L: And I rejoice over the arrival of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus, because these have filled up your lack; \v 18 for they refreshed my spirit and yours.
en.B: It makes me glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus are here, because they have filled the gap your absence left. \v 18 They have refreshed me in spirit, and you as well.
en.R: I am happy that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus came here. I could not be with all of you, but having them here was almost like having you. \v 18 They have cheered me up, just as they cheered you up.

fr.L: Et je me réjouis de la venue de Stéphanas, de Fortunat et d’Achaïque, parce que ceux-ci ont comblé votre manque ; \v 18 car ils ont réconforté mon esprit et le vôtre.
fr.B: Je suis heureux que Stéphanas, Fortunat et Achaïque soient ici, car ils ont comblé le vide que votre absence laissait. \v 18 Ils ont réconforté mon esprit, et le vôtre aussi.
fr.R: Je suis content que Stéphanas, Fortunat et Achaïque soient venus ici. Je ne pouvais pas être avec vous tous, mais en les ayant ici, c’était presque comme si vous étiez là. \v 18 Ils m’ont redonné du courage, comme ils vous en ont redonné à vous aussi.

es.L: Y me alegro por la venida de Estéfanas, de Fortunato y de Acaico, porque estos han suplido {{plural_you:la falta de ustedes|vuestra falta}}; \v 18 pues han confortado mi espíritu y el {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}}.
es.B: Me alegra que Estéfanas, Fortunato y Acaico estén aquí, porque han llenado el vacío que dejaba {{plural_you:la ausencia de ustedes|vuestra ausencia}}. \v 18 Me han reanimado el espíritu, y a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} también.
es.R: Estoy contento de que Estéfanas, Fortunato y Acaico hayan venido. Yo no podía estar con todos {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, pero tenerlos aquí ha sido casi como {{plural_you:tenerlos|teneros}} a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. \v 18 Me han animado mucho, igual que {{plural_you:los|os}} animaron a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

sw.L: Nami nafurahi kwa kuja kwa Stefana na Fortunato na Akaiko, kwa sababu hawa wamejaza upungufu wenu; \v 18 kwa maana wameiburudisha roho yangu na yenu.
sw.B: Ninafurahi kwamba Stefana, Fortunato na Akaiko wako hapa, kwa sababu wamejaza pengo lililoachwa na kutokuwepo kwenu. \v 18 Wameniburudisha rohoni, na ninyi pia.
sw.R: Ninafurahi kwamba Stefana, Fortunato na Akaiko walikuja hapa. Sikuweza kuwa pamoja nanyi nyote, lakini kuwa nao hapa kulikuwa karibu sawa na kuwa nanyi. \v 18 Wamenitia moyo, kama walivyowatia moyo ninyi pia.

vi.L: Tôi vui mừng vì Sê-pha-na, Phốt-tu-na và A-chai-cơ đã đến, vì những người này đã bù đắp sự vắng mặt của anh chị em; \v 18 vì họ đã làm cho tâm linh tôi và [tâm linh] anh chị em được tươi mới.
vi.B: Tôi vui mừng vì Sê-pha-na, Phốt-tu-na và A-chai-cơ đã đến đây, vì họ đã lấp chỗ trống mà sự vắng mặt của anh chị em để lại. \v 18 Họ đã làm cho tâm linh tôi được tươi mới, và cả anh chị em cũng vậy.
vi.R: Tôi vui vì Sê-pha-na, Phốt-tu-na và A-chai-cơ đã đến đây. Tôi không thể ở với tất cả anh chị em, nhưng có họ ở đây thì gần như có anh chị em vậy. \v 18 Họ đã làm cho tôi được phấn khởi, cũng như họ đã làm cho anh chị em được phấn khởi.

ko.L: 나는 스데바나와 브드나도와 아가이고가 온 것을 기뻐합니다. 그들이 여러분의 부족한 것을 채웠기 때문입니다. \v 18 그들은 나의 영과 여러분의 [영]을 새롭게 했습니다.
ko.B: 스데바나와 브드나도와 아가이고가 이곳에 와서 나는 기쁩니다. 여러분이 없어서 생긴 빈자리를 그들이 채워 주었습니다. \v 18 그들은 내 마음을 새롭게 해 주었고, 여러분의 마음도 그렇게 해 주었습니다.
ko.R: 스데바나와 브드나도와 아가이고가 이곳에 와서 나는 기쁩니다. 나는 여러분 모두와 함께 있을 수 없지만, 그들이 여기 있으니 여러분이 있는 것과 거의 같았습니다. \v 18 그들은 여러분의 마음을 기쁘게 해 주었듯이 내 마음도 기쁘게 해 주었습니다.

pt.L: E eu me alegro com a vinda de Estéfanas e de Fortunato e de Acaico, porque eles supriram a falta de vocês; \v 18 pois deram descanso ao meu espírito e ao de vocês.
pt.B: Fico feliz por Estéfanas, Fortunato e Acaico estarem aqui, porque eles preencheram o vazio que a ausência de vocês deixou. \v 18 Eles reanimaram o meu espírito, e o de vocês também.
pt.R: Estou contente porque Estéfanas, Fortunato e Acaico vieram até aqui. Eu não podia estar com todos vocês, mas ter esses irmãos aqui foi quase como ter vocês. \v 18 Eles me animaram, assim como animaram vocês.

decisions.choice: three men from Corinth who came to Paul in Ephesus
decisions.reason: They probably brought the Corinthians' letter (7:1) and would take this one back. Fortunatus is a Latin name and Achaicus means "man of Achaia"; such names were often given to slaves or freed slaves, so they may have belonged to Stephanas's household, but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: arrival, presence
decisions.reason: παρουσίᾳ is the ordinary word for someone's arrival or presence. Paul uses it of Christ's coming in 15:23, but here of these men.

decisions.choice: your lack: Paul's not having the church with him
alternatives: what you failed to do for me
decisions.reason: ὑστέρημα is what is missing. Paul most likely means that their visit made up for his separation from the church, not that the church had failed him.

decisions.choice: refreshed: gave new strength and rest
decisions.reason: ἀνέπαυσαν is to give rest or relief (2 Corinthians 7:13; Philemon 7, 20). "And yours" probably means that the church too was refreshed by their faithful service, or will be when they bring Paul's reply.

decisions.choice: filled the gap your absence left (B); I could not be with all of you, but having them here was almost like having you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was lacking (m3).

decisions.choice: Fortunat, Achaïque
decisions.reason: The usual French forms of the two names, as French writes Épaïnète and Aquilas.

decisions.choice: "Phốt-tu-na", "A-chai-cơ", "A-chai", "Sê-pha-na"
decisions.reason: The names in the Protestant transliterations, as the style guide asks.

es.B: {{plural_you:Procuren|Procurad}}, pues, que personas como estas sean honradas.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:muestren|mostrad}} respeto a personas como ellos.

sw.L: Basi watambueni watu kama hao.

sw.R: Kwa hiyo waonyesheni heshima watu kama wao.

vi.L: Vậy hãy công nhận những người như thế.
vi.B: Vậy hãy lo sao cho những người như thế được tôn trọng.
vi.R: Vậy hãy tỏ lòng kính trọng những người như họ.

ko.R: 그러니 그들 같은 사람들을 존경하십시오.

pt.L: Portanto, reconheçam tais [pessoas].
pt.B: Façam questão, então, de honrar pessoas como essas.
pt.R: Por isso, mostrem respeito por pessoas como eles.

decisions.choice: recognize: acknowledge their worth and honor them
decisions.reason: ἐπιγινώσκετε here means to give due recognition, as 1 Thessalonians 5:12 asks for those who labor among the believers.

en.L: The churches of Asia greet you.

en.R: The churches in the province of Asia say hello.

fr.R: Les églises de la province d’Asie vous disent bonjour.

es.R: Las iglesias de la provincia de Asia {{plural_you:les|os}} mandan saludos.

sw.R: Makanisa ya jimbo la Asia yanawasalimu.

vi.L: Các Hội Thánh ở A-si chào anh chị em.
vi.B: Các Hội Thánh ở A-si gửi lời chào anh chị em.
vi.R: Các Hội Thánh ở tỉnh A-si gửi lời chào anh chị em.

ko.B: 아시아의 교회들이 여러분에게 문안합니다.
ko.R: 아시아 지방의 교회들이 여러분에게 안부를 전합니다.

pt.L: As igrejas da Ásia saúdam vocês.
pt.B: As igrejas da Ásia mandam saudações a vocês.
pt.R: As igrejas da província da Ásia mandam lembranças a vocês.

decisions.choice: Asia: the Roman province in the west of what is now Turkey
decisions.reason: Ephesus was its chief city. From there the gospel spread through the province (Acts 19:10), to churches such as Colossae and Laodicea (Colossians 4:13-16).

decisions.choice: the province of Asia
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that a Roman province is meant (m1).

decisions.choice: say hello
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for a greeting, as in Colossians 4:10.

decisions.choice: "A-si" (L, B), "tỉnh A-si" (R)
decisions.reason: The form of the Vietnamese Romans 16:5: the Roman province, not the continent.

decisions.choice: "문안합니다" (L, B); "안부를 전합니다" (R) for the greetings, through verses 19-21; "거룩한 입맞춤"
decisions.reason: The words of Romans 16:16-23 for those who send greetings.

source.text: ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς ἐν κυρίῳ πολλὰ Ἀκύλας καὶ Πρίσκα σὺν τῇ κατ’ οἶκον αὐτῶν ἐκκλησίᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: Greet you in [the] Lord much Aquila and Prisca with the at house of them church.

en.L: Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in [the] Lord, with the church at their house.
en.B: Warm greetings in the Lord from Aquila and Prisca and from the church that meets in their house.
en.R: Aquila and Prisca, who belong to the Lord as you do, send you warm greetings. So does the church that meets in their home.

fr.L: Aquilas et Prisca vous saluent chaleureusement dans le Seigneur, avec l’église qui [est] dans leur maison.
fr.B: Aquilas et Prisca vous adressent de chaleureuses salutations dans le Seigneur, ainsi que l’église qui se réunit chez eux.
fr.R: Aquilas et Prisca, qui appartiennent au Seigneur comme vous, vous envoient leurs salutations chaleureuses. L’église qui se réunit dans leur maison vous salue aussi.

es.L: {{plural_you:Los|Os}} saludan mucho en [el] Señor Aquila y Prisca, con la iglesia que [se reúne] en su casa.
es.B: Muchos saludos en el Señor de parte de Aquila y Prisca, y de la iglesia que se reúne en su casa.
es.R: Aquila y Prisca, que pertenecen al Señor como {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} mandan muchos saludos. También la iglesia que se reúne en su casa.

sw.L: Akila na Priska pamoja na kanisa lililo nyumbani mwao wanawasalimu sana katika Bwana.
sw.B: Akila na Priska, pamoja na kanisa linalokutana nyumbani mwao, wanawasalimu sana katika Bwana.
sw.R: Akila na Priska, ambao ni wa Bwana kama ninyi, wanawatumia salamu nyingi. Vilevile kanisa linalokutana nyumbani kwao linawasalimu.

vi.L: A-qui-la và Bê-rít-ca, cùng với Hội Thánh nhóm tại nhà họ, chào anh chị em rất nhiều trong Chúa.
vi.B: A-qui-la và Bê-rít-ca, cùng với Hội Thánh nhóm họp tại nhà họ, gửi lời chào thân thiết đến anh chị em trong Chúa.
vi.R: A-qui-la và Bê-rít-ca, là những người cũng thuộc về Chúa như anh chị em, gửi lời chào thân thiết đến anh chị em. Hội Thánh nhóm họp tại nhà họ cũng vậy.

ko.L: 아굴라와 브리스가가 그들의 집에 있는 교회와 함께 주님 안에서 여러분에게 많이 문안합니다.
ko.B: 아굴라와 브리스가와 그들의 집에서 모이는 교회가 주님 안에서 여러분에게 따뜻하게 문안합니다.
ko.R: 여러분처럼 주님께 속한 아굴라와 브리스가가 여러분에게 따뜻한 안부를 전합니다. 그들의 집에서 모이는 교회도 안부를 전합니다.

pt.L: Áquila e Prisca saúdam muito vocês no Senhor, com a igreja [que está] na casa deles.
pt.B: Áquila e Prisca, junto com a igreja que se reúne na casa deles, mandam a vocês muitas saudações no Senhor.
pt.R: Áquila e Prisca, que pertencem ao Senhor como vocês, mandam saudações carinhosas. A igreja que se reúne na casa deles também.

decisions.choice: Aquila and Prisca: a Jewish couple who had worked with Paul in Corinth
decisions.reason: They met Paul in Corinth after Claudius expelled the Jews from Rome, worked with him at tentmaking, and then went with him to Ephesus (Acts 18:1-3, 18-26). The Corinthians knew them well. Acts calls her Priscilla, the familiar form of the name; Paul calls her Prisca (Romans 16:3).

decisions.choice: the church in their house: believers who met in their home
decisions.reason: The first churches met in homes (Romans 16:5; Colossians 4:15). In Ephesus, as later in Rome, a group met in the couple's house.

decisions.choice: warmly, in the Lord: the greeting of fellow believers
decisions.reason: πολλὰ ("much") makes the greeting warm, and "in the Lord" marks it as the greeting of people who belong to the Lord together.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: the greeting ends with the church in their house
alternatives: some manuscripts add "with whom I am staying"
decisions.reason: Some Greek-Latin manuscripts add that Paul was lodging with Aquila and Prisca, which fits Acts 18:3 but is not in the older manuscripts. Some manuscripts also spell her name Priscilla, as in Acts. (From general knowledge of the manuscripts; reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.)

decisions.choice: Prisca
decisions.reason: The levels keep Paul's form of the name, as in Romans 16:3 (m1).

decisions.choice: the church that meets in their house (B); home (R)
decisions.reason: The church is the people, not the building; "meets" says so, as in Romans 16:5.

decisions.choice: who belong to the Lord as you do
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in the Lord" adds to the greeting (m3).

decisions.choice: Priska
decisions.reason: "Priska" as in Swahili Romans 16:3, following the form of the name Paul uses; Acts 18 calls her by the longer form "Prisila".

decisions.choice: "Bê-rít-ca" for Prisca; "A-qui-la"
decisions.reason: The form of the Vietnamese Romans 16:3 and 2 Timothy 4:19, where the Greek also has Prisca.

decisions.choice: Prisca
decisions.reason: Brazilian readers know her as Priscila, the form Acts uses; Paul writes the shorter Prisca, and every level keeps his form, as the English does (m1).

source.text: ἀσπάζονται ὑμᾶς οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πάντες.

en.L: All the {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} greet you.

es.R: Todos los creyentes de aquí {{plural_you:les|os}} mandan saludos.

sw.R: Waumini wote walioko hapa wanawatumia salamu zao.

vi.R: Tất cả các tín hữu ở đây gửi lời chào anh chị em.

ko.L: 모든 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}가 여러분에게 문안합니다.
ko.B: 이곳의 모든 {{gender:형제자매|형제}}가 여러분에게 문안합니다.
ko.R: 이곳의 모든 신자들이 여러분에게 안부를 전합니다.

pt.L: Todos os {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}} saúdam vocês.
pt.B: Todos os {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}} daqui mandam saudações a vocês.
pt.R: Todos os que creem em Jesus aqui mandam saudações a vocês.

decisions.choice: all the believers where Paul is, women and men
decisions.reason: After the churches of Asia and the church in Aquila and Prisca's house, "all the brothers" is most likely the believers in Ephesus as a whole.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The believers included women and men. Readable says "believers", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: here
decisions.reason: Those who send greetings are the believers where Paul is writing (m1).

source.text: ἀσπάσασθε ἀλλήλους ἐν φιλήματι ἁγίῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Greet one another with kiss holy.

en.L: Greet one another with a holy kiss.
en.B: Greet one another with a holy kiss.
en.R: When you greet each other, give each other a holy kiss.

fr.L: Saluez-vous les uns les autres par un saint baiser.
fr.B: Saluez-vous les uns les autres d’un saint baiser.
fr.R: Quand vous vous saluez, donnez-vous les uns aux autres un saint baiser.

es.L: {{plural_you:Salúdense|Saludaos}} unos a otros con un beso santo.
es.B: {{plural_you:Salúdense|Saludaos}} unos a otros con un beso santo.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:se saluden|os saludéis}}, {{plural_you:dense|daos}} unos a otros un beso santo.

sw.L: Salimianeni kwa busu takatifu.
sw.B: Salimianeni ninyi kwa ninyi kwa busu takatifu.
sw.R: Mnaposalimiana, mpeane busu takatifu.

vi.B: Hãy chào nhau bằng cái hôn thánh.
vi.R: Khi chào nhau, hãy trao cho nhau cái hôn thánh.

ko.L: 거룩한 입맞춤으로 서로 문안하십시오.

decisions.choice: a holy kiss: the greeting of family members, shared by believers as God's family
decisions.reason: A kiss on the cheek was a common greeting between relatives and close friends in the ancient Mediterranean world. Believers greeted one another this way as members of one family (Romans 16:16; 2 Corinthians 13:12; 1 Thessalonians 5:26; 1 Peter 5:14). "Holy" marks it as belonging to God's people, pure and without romantic meaning. In a church divided into parties (1:10-12), the command is pointed.

decisions.choice: accursed: under God's curse, handed over to destruction
decisions.reason: ἀνάθεμα is the word of 12:3: what the Greek Old Testament calls devoted to destruction (Deuteronomy 7:26). Paul uses it for one cut off and under God's curse (Romans 9:3; Galatians 1:8-9).

decisions.choice: love: heartfelt love and loyalty
decisions.reason: Paul usually uses another verb for love; φιλεῖ is the word for warm affection between friends. Its use here may come from a set form of words used in worship. To not love the Lord is to have no part with him.

decisions.choice: a solemn curse formula, leaving judgment to God
decisions.reason: ἤτω is a third-person command, "let him be". It solemnly declares that whoever does not love the Lord stands under God's judgment; it does not call on the readers to act. The prayer that follows asks for the Lord who will judge to come (4:5).

decisions.choice: the Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: The next sentence prays for "our Lord" to come, and verse 23 names him: the Lord Jesus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: "Anyone" includes women and men; Balanced and Readable need no pronoun.

decisions.choice: A curse on (B); May God's curse be on (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "accursed" and Balanced and Readable "curse", the words of 12:3 ("Jesus is cursed"). Readable says whose curse it is (m1).

decisions.choice: "quelqu’un … qu’il soit maudit" (L), with no gender setting; maudit (L, B), la malédiction de Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:them|him}} at Literal; in French "quelqu’un" already means anyone, and the "il" that refers back to it is ordinary generic French, so no span is used. "Anathème" copies the Greek word but is church jargon; "maudit" says the sense (m1) and matches the curse of 12:3.

decisions.choice: sea anatema (L); maldito sea (B); la maldición de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: The word means placed under God's curse (m1). Literal keeps "anatema", the Greek word that Spanish has borrowed; Balanced and Readable say "maldito", "maldición". "El que" and "alguno" cover anyone, so the English gender span has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: awe chini ya laana (L); Laana iwe juu ya (B); Mungu amlaani (R)
decisions.reason: Under God's curse, judgment left to God (meaning decisions); Readable names God, as the English Readable. The verb prefix a- means he or she, so the English Literal gender span has no Swahili counterpart.

decisions.choice: "bị nguyền rủa" for anathema, as in 12:3
decisions.reason: The word of the Vietnamese Galatians 1:8. "Người ấy" needs no gender span.

decisions.choice: "사랑하다" for the verb of warm affection here; "저주를 받다" for being accursed, as in 12:3
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that the verb is the word for warm affection between friends, not the usual word; Korean has one word for love, "사랑하다", which covers both.

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English Literal needs a setting for "them/him". Portuguese "se alguém ... seja amaldiçoado" has no pronoun, and the masculine form after "alguém" is the ordinary generic Portuguese for anyone (style section 7), so no setting is used.

sw.L: Marana tha!
sw.B: Bwana wetu, njoo!
sw.R: Bwana wetu Yesu, njoo!

vi.R: Lạy Chúa Giê-xu của chúng con, xin hãy đến!

ko.B: 우리 주님, 오십시오!
ko.R: 우리 주 예수님, 오십시오!

pt.L: Maranata!
pt.B: Nosso Senhor, vem!
pt.R: Nosso Senhor Jesus, vem!

decisions.choice: an Aramaic prayer, kept in its original language
decisions.reason: Μαράνα θά is Aramaic, the language of the first believers in Judea, written in Greek letters. Paul does not translate it, so the Corinthians already knew it, probably from worship. The Didache, an early Christian writing, has the same words in a prayer at the Lord's Supper (Didache 10:6).

decisions.choice: a prayer: "Our Lord, come!"
decisions.reason: Ancient manuscripts were written without spaces between words, so the division is an editor's decision. The SBLGNT divides the letters as Μαράνα θά, which means "Our Lord, come!". Divided another way they mean "Our Lord has come" or "is coming". The prayer "Come, Lord Jesus" in Revelation 22:20 and the Lord's Supper kept "until he comes" (11:26) favor the prayer, but the statement is possible.

decisions.choice: the earliest believers prayed to Jesus as Lord
decisions.reason: The words come from the Aramaic-speaking church, before the gospel reached the Greek world. Already there believers called Jesus "our Lord" and prayed to him to come.

decisions.choice: Marana tha (L); Our Lord, come (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic words, as Galatians 4:6 keeps "Abba", written in English letters with the SBLGNT's division into two words. Balanced and Readable give the meaning (m2).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: The Lord prayed to is Jesus, named in verse 23 and in Revelation 22:20.

decisions.choice: "Ma-ra-na-tha" (L); "Lạy Chúa chúng con, xin hãy đến" (B); "Lạy Chúa Giê-xu của chúng con, xin hãy đến" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Aramaic in the transliteration readers know; Balanced and Readable give it as a prayer (m2), with "Lạy Chúa" and "chúng con", the style guide's forms for believers praying to the Lord.

decisions.choice: "마라나 타" (L), the Aramaic in Hangul; "우리 주님, 오십시오!" (B, R), in 합쇼체 to the Lord
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the Aramaic, divided as the SBLGNT divides it, as a prayer, "Our Lord, come!", uncertain and footnoted. The prayer speaks to the Lord, so Korean uses 합쇼체 ("오십시오"), as believers speak to Jesus.

decisions.choice: Maranata
decisions.reason: Aramaic words are written as Portuguese writes their sounds (style section 11), and Portuguese has long written this prayer as one word, "Maranata". The one-word spelling does not decide the division of the letters: the meaning "Our Lord, come!" that Balanced and Readable give follows the SBLGNT's division (m2).

decisions.choice: vem (tu)
decisions.reason: The prayer speaks to Jesus, so it uses "tu" (style section 4): "vem" is the "tu" imperative. "Venha" would be the "você" form.

decisions.choice: a prayer: may grace be with you
alternatives: a statement: grace is with you
decisions.reason: There is no verb. As in the closing of Paul's other letters, it is a blessing prayed over the readers (2 Corinthians 13:13; Philippians 4:23).

decisions.choice: the letter ends where it began, with the grace of the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Paul opened with grace and peace (1:3) and thanked God for the grace given in Christ (1:4). After a curse on those who do not love the Lord, the last word is his grace.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the Lord Jesus"

decisions.choice: Paul's love for all of them, without exception
decisions.reason: There is no verb: it may be a wish ("be with") or a statement ("is with"). Paul ends no other letter with his own love. After a letter that rebuked the church sharply, he assures every one of them, whatever party they took (1:12), of his love.

decisions.choice: in Christ Jesus: Paul's love belongs to their shared life in Christ
alternatives: only describing "you": you who are in Christ
decisions.reason: The phrase goes with the whole sentence: Paul loves them as one who, like them, belongs to Christ Jesus.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "Amen" at the end
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "Amen", as copyists often did at the end of a book, and the King James Version has it. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)

decisions.choice: I send my love to
